newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine '96 refined sugar output 3.26 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine '96 refined sugar output 3.26 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine's refined sugar output this year will reach 3.26 million tonnes, including 2.70 million tonnes from this year's sugar beet harvest and 561,000 tonnes from raws imports, a top industry official said on Monday.

"Total sugar output from our sugar beet harvest this year will be 2.70 million tonnes," Olexander Bohatarenyk, deputy head of the state sugar concern UkrSukor told Reuters, revising down slightly his November forecast of 2.80 million tonnes.
"We have refined 3.224 million tonnes to date. That includes 2.66 million tonnes of whites refined from this year's sugar beet harvest," he said. Raws imports had been refined earlier in the year.
Ukraine's refined sugar output in 1995 was 3.49 million tonnes.
Bohatarenyk said about 30 of 191 refineries were operating and had refined 23.1 million tonnes of sugar beets -- down from 29.9 million tonnes at this time last year.
The refineries would complete their work in January.
"The sugar market in Ukraine has died because there is a surplus of sugar," he said. "Sugar is being given away in place of salaries and it is being bartered for fuel and equipment."
Bohatarenyk said the industry hoped for improvements next year when supplies would fall and demand would increase.
He said the government, which previously forecast refined sugar output at 3.30 million tonnes, had maintained its forecast that exports would total 1.50 million tonnes of sugar.
Ukraine's traditional buyer Russia also had a surplus of sugar on its market.
"We still expect a significant portion of our sugar to go to Russia, and the rest to our other neighbours," he said.
Ukraine also expects to export sugar to Kazakhstan, Belarus and Baltic countries.
Russia imposed a quota of 1.15 million tonnes on Ukraine earlier this month to prevent what it called dumping of cheaper Ukrainian supplies on its market.
